newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end higher, outperforming others.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end higher, outperforming others.

text.p: Madrid stocks ended stronger on Tuesday with buying interest in all different sectors despite a weaker trend in main foreign markets, dealers said.
They said the underlying trend in Spain's equity market was really strong, but after the latest rally they did not rule out the possibility of a forthcoming consolidation.
The general index was up 5.70 points, 1.05 percent, to 547.56 and the Ibex-35 gained 71.17 points, 1.14 percent, to 6,299.85.
"Morgan Stanley's news supported the market," a dealer in Madrid said.

Brokerage house Morgan Stanley said on Tuesday it had upgraded Spain's weighting to 4.5 percent from 3.0 percent in its European model portfolio, based on increased expectations of Spain's timely entry into EMU.
The brokerage's model portfolio bought Endesa, which ended more than two percent higher. Gas Natural rose 5.55 percent.
Among banking stocks Santander gained 25 pesetas to 4,045, while Bankinter was 1.6 percent up at 6,090.
Telefonica rose 25 pesetas to 4.045, while Repsol added 100 pesetas to 6,090.
